12	
13	## Intent
14	
15	**Problem:** Entries from text/audio/photo capture (Epic 3) are invisible — "Meus Registros" is still the Epic 1 placeholder, and `EntriesRepository` only has `create`.
16	
17	**Approach:** Replace the placeholder with a screen listing every Entry, newest first, grouped by day, each card marked by origin. Extend `EntriesRepository` with paginated `list()`, falling back to Hive when offline. No sync badge, no tap-to-detail, no search/filter — those are 4.2/4.4/Epic 5.
18	
19	## Boundaries & Constraints
20	
21	**Always:**
22	- `EntriesRepository.list({cursor, limit = 20})` → `Either<Failure, EntriesPage>`. Server assumed newest-first by `occurredAt` (undocumented, decided per AGENTS.md policy).
23	- `networkOffline`/`networkTimeout` → fall back to a full `entries` Hive box dump, sorted `occurredAt` desc, `nextCursor: null`. Other failures propagate as `Left`.
24	- Successful page persists to the Hive box, same "persist then return" shape `create()` uses.
25	- Group by `occurredAt.toLocal()` truncated to day, never `createdAt`. Grouping fn is pure Dart (no flutter import, RNF06) in `entries/domain`; day labels are presentation's job.
26	- Card spine by `EntrySource`, exact hex match to prototype's `sourceMeta`: manual→`colorPrimary`, audio→`colorSecondary`, photo→`colorTextSecondary`, chat→`colorAccent`. Plus source icon, time, excerpt. No badge, not tappable.
27	- Skeleton only past 300ms (mirror `BootSplashScreen`'s `Timer` pattern), new generic `SkeletonBox` in `lib/core/widgets/` built only from existing tokens — no new colors.
28	- `MeusRegistrosCubit` gets its own sealed state, never `Resource<T>` (its doc comment excludes RF07). `lazySingleton` in `registerEntriesFeature()`.
29	- Global `ExpiryOverlayHost` already covers this screen; just confirm this screen's `ScrollController`/cubit aren't torn down under it.
30	
31	**Ask First:** None — open calls are pinned above.
32	
33	**Never:** sync badge (4.2), tap/detail nav (4.4), filters/search (Epic 5, tags), pull-to-refresh, any repository method beyond `list`/`create`, polished empty-state CTA (4.3 — plain "no entries" text only).
34	
35	## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
36	
37	| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
38	|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
39	| First load, online | Screen opens | Skeleton past 300ms, then grouped list | N/A |
40	| Scroll pagination | Near list end, `nextCursor != null` | Next page appended, no dup ids | Fetch failure keeps current items + inline retry |
41	| Offline fallback | `list()` returns offline/timeout | Cached entries shown, sorted desc | N/A |
42	| Other failure | e.g. `authExpired` | Error state rendered | Global overlay or inline retry |
43	| Zero entries | Empty page + empty cache | Plain "no entries yet" text | N/A |

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** Entries from text/audio/photo capture (Epic 3) are invisible — "Meus Registros" is still the Epic 1 placeholder, and `EntriesRepository` only has `create`.

**Approach:** Replace the placeholder with a screen listing every Entry, newest first, grouped by day, each card marked by origin. Extend `EntriesRepository` with paginated `list()`, falling back to Hive when offline. No sync badge, no tap-to-detail, no search/filter — those are 4.2/4.4/Epic 5.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- `EntriesRepository.list({cursor, limit = 20})` → `Either<Failure, EntriesPage>`. Server assumed newest-first by `occurredAt` (undocumented, decided per AGENTS.md policy).
- `networkOffline`/`networkTimeout` → fall back to a full `entries` Hive box dump, sorted `occurredAt` desc, `nextCursor: null`. Other failures propagate as `Left`.
- Successful page persists to the Hive box, same "persist then return" shape `create()` uses.
- Group by `occurredAt.toLocal()` truncated to day, never `createdAt`. Grouping fn is pure Dart (no flutter import, RNF06) in `entries/domain`; day labels are presentation's job.
- Card spine by `EntrySource`, exact hex match to prototype's `sourceMeta`: manual→`colorPrimary`, audio→`colorSecondary`, photo→`colorTextSecondary`, chat→`colorAccent`. Plus source icon, time, excerpt. No badge, not tappable.
- Skeleton only past 300ms (mirror `BootSplashScreen`'s `Timer` pattern), new generic `SkeletonBox` in `lib/core/widgets/` built only from existing tokens — no new colors.
- `MeusRegistrosCubit` gets its own sealed state, never `Resource<T>` (its doc comment excludes RF07). `lazySingleton` in `registerEntriesFeature()`.
- Global `ExpiryOverlayHost` already covers this screen; just confirm this screen's `ScrollController`/cubit aren't torn down under it.

**Ask First:** None — open calls are pinned above.

**Never:** sync badge (4.2), tap/detail nav (4.4), filters/search (Epic 5, tags), pull-to-refresh, any repository method beyond `list`/`create`, polished empty-state CTA (4.3 — plain "no entries" text only).

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| First load, online | Screen opens | Skeleton past 300ms, then grouped list | N/A |
| Scroll pagination | Near list end, `nextCursor != null` | Next page appended, no dup ids | Fetch failure keeps current items + inline retry |
| Offline fallback | `list()` returns offline/timeout | Cached entries shown, sorted desc | N/A |
| Other failure | e.g. `authExpired` | Error state rendered | Global overlay or inline retry |
| Zero entries | Empty page + empty cache | Plain "no entries yet" text | N/A |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `entries/domain/repositories/entries_repository.dart` -- add `list()` to the one-method port
- `entries/domain/entities/entry.dart` -- `occurredAt` stays raw ISO string, parsed only for grouping
- `entries/data/repositories/entries_repository_impl.dart` -- `create()`'s mirror shape for `list()`
- `entries/data/datasources/entries_remote_data_source.dart` -- `create()`'s call/error-map shape to mirror
- `entries/entries_injection.dart` -- add `MeusRegistrosCubit` registration
- `lib/core/network/api_client.dart` -- `get(function, {queryParameters})` already fits
- `lib/core/failure/failure.dart` -- `networkOffline`/`networkTimeout` = fallback triggers
- `lib/core/resource.dart` -- doc excludes RF07 from `Resource<T>`
- `app_router.dart:118-120`, `placeholder_screens.dart:159-182` -- route + placeholder
- `placeholder_screens.dart:355-397` (`_KanbanCard`) -- spine-card structure to mirror
- `placeholder_screens.dart:18-58` (`BootSplashScreen`) -- 300ms skeleton-delay pattern
- `lib/core/widgets/back_arrow_header.dart` -- reused as-is

30	+# Epic 4 Context: Timeline & History
31	+
32	+<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->
33	+
34	+## Goal
35	+
36	+Users can see every Entry they've ever captured, from any source (text, audio, photo), in one chronological view grouped by date, each carrying a live per-entry sync status — and never lose track of something they wrote, even offline or mid-session-expiry. This is the first independently demoable milestone built on top of the `entries` feature Epic 3 introduced: a working, origin-marked timeline with reconciling sync badges, with no search or filtering yet (that's Epic 5). Depends on Epic 3 (there is nothing to list until Entries exist).
37	+
38	+## Stories
39	+
40	+- Story 4.1: Chronological Entry List with Origin Marking
41	+- Story 4.2: Per-Entry Sync Badge
42	+- Story 4.3: Empty-State Handling
43	+- Story 4.4: Entry Detail View
44	+
45	+## Requirements & Constraints
46	+
47	+- All Entries from every source are listed together in one list, grouped by date, each visually marked with its origin.
48	+- A list load that exceeds the loading-indicator threshold (300ms) shows a skeleton loading state; under that threshold, no loading UI appears at all.
49	+- Zero Entries renders a dedicated empty state with a path back to capture — never a blank list.
50	+- A single Entry can be opened to view its full content; there is no edit affordance anywhere on that screen, and no update/delete capability exists for Entries at all — read-only, permanently.
51	+- A detail request for an Entry that doesn't exist or belongs to another user returns a generic not-found outcome, never a distinguishable permission-denied code; the UI must treat both identically.
52	+- The sync badge has exactly three states (Synchronizing / Synchronization error / Synchronized), derived client-side only — the backend has no sync-status field. A freshly created Entry starts Synchronizing until the write is confirmed, then flips to Synchronized. A failed write (network or any error code) shows Synchronization error until a later successful write reconciles it.
53	+- Tapping an error badge retries that Entry's write when the underlying error is retryable; when it isn't, it shows an inline explanation instead — never a dead retry button.
54	+- The sync-badge update stream is fully independent of the auth/session stream: a pending sync transition is never blocked, delayed, or cleared by session-expiry handling, and the session-expiry overlay must be able to appear over this screen without crashing or losing scroll position.
55	+- This feature's screen composes three data streams (auth status, sync-badge state, Entry data) only through the domain layer — no BLoC/Cubit here ever references another BLoC/Cubit directly.
56	+- No swipe gesture is implemented on a record card (Entries are immutable, so no gesture may imply an edit/delete that doesn't exist).
57	+- Color is never the sole carrier of sync-badge state — always paired with an accessible label, and the retry hit area must be ≥44pt even though the dot itself is small.
58	+
59	+## Technical Decisions
60	+
61	+- `entries/domain` (introduced in Epic 3) already owns the `Entry` entity, the `EntriesRepository` port, and the Hive box; this epic extends that same port with read/list operations rather than introducing a second Entry model or owner.
62	+- `EntriesRepository` exposes create and read only, permanently — no update/delete method is ever added, matching the backend's lack of a mutating entries endpoint.
63	+- One single derivation function lives in `entries/domain` computing the sync badge from `Entry.serverRevision`, `Entry.updatedAt`, and transient per-entry write state (no pending write → Synchronized; write in flight → Synchronizing; failed write → Synchronization error). Every screen that ever renders this badge (this timeline now, chat's save confirmation later) consumes that one function's output — none recomputes it inline.
64	+- This screen's composite state (auth × sync × data) is its own sealed state class, not the shared generic single-fetch `Resource<T>` type used elsewhere — it has a composite, multi-stream lifecycle `Resource<T>` isn't meant for.
65	+- Reads fall back transparently to the local Hive cache when offline; the cache stores exactly what the server returned, keyed by id — never locally filtered, joined, sorted, or re-derived. Pagination uses the server's own cursor convention verbatim, cached alongside the box it pages.
66	+- A badge retry re-attempts the same underlying write call that originally failed; there is no separate retry endpoint for entries.
67	+
68	+## UX & Interaction Patterns
69	+
70	+- Record card spine color encodes origin: manual = primary color, audio = olive green, photo = gray (chat's accent color is reserved for Epic 6's chat-saved entries).
71	+- The prototype shows the record card as otherwise display-only — tapping it previously did nothing beyond surfacing the badge's retry affordance in the error state. The detail view this epic adds (FR-18) has no prototype precedent; build it minimal and strictly read-only, consistent with the record card's established "no edit/expand implied" convention.
72	+- Skeleton rows use the shared skeleton-loading component (never a spinner) and only appear past the 300ms threshold.
73	+- Empty state must offer a concrete CTA back into the capture flow (opens the Insertion Modal), not just explanatory copy.
74	+
75	+## Cross-Story Dependencies
76	+
77	+- Depends on Epic 3: the `entries` feature, `Entry` entity, `EntriesRepository.create`, and the entries Hive box must already exist; this epic only adds read/list.
78	+- Reuses Epic 1's session-expiry overlay (FR-2) as-is for mid-timeline session expiry — no new overlay is built here.
79	+- The sync-badge derivation function built in Story 4.2 is a shared dependency: Epic 6 (chat's save-to-journal confirmation) consumes the same function rather than building its own.
80	+- Epic 5 (Semantic Search & Filtering) is built directly on top of this epic's timeline surface and extends the same `EntriesRepository` port further with search — do not duplicate list/display logic there.

99	+## Intent
100	+
101	+**Problem:** Entries from text/audio/photo capture (Epic 3) are invisible — "Meus Registros" is still the Epic 1 placeholder, and `EntriesRepository` only has `create`.
102	+
103	+**Approach:** Replace the placeholder with a screen listing every Entry, newest first, grouped by day, each card marked by origin. Extend `EntriesRepository` with paginated `list()`, falling back to Hive when offline. No sync badge, no tap-to-detail, no search/filter — those are 4.2/4.4/Epic 5.
104	+
105	+## Boundaries & Constraints
106	+
107	+**Always:**
108	+- `EntriesRepository.list({cursor, limit = 20})` → `Either<Failure, EntriesPage>`. Server assumed newest-first by `occurredAt` (undocumented, decided per AGENTS.md policy).
109	+- `networkOffline`/`networkTimeout` → fall back to a full `entries` Hive box dump, sorted `occurredAt` desc, `nextCursor: null`. Other failures propagate as `Left`.
110	+- Successful page persists to the Hive box, same "persist then return" shape `create()` uses.
111	+- Group by `occurredAt.toLocal()` truncated to day, never `createdAt`. Grouping fn is pure Dart (no flutter import, RNF06) in `entries/domain`; day labels are presentation's job.
112	+- Card spine by `EntrySource`, exact hex match to prototype's `sourceMeta`: manual→`colorPrimary`, audio→`colorSecondary`, photo→`colorTextSecondary`, chat→`colorAccent`. Plus source icon, time, excerpt. No badge, not tappable.
113	+- Skeleton only past 300ms (mirror `BootSplashScreen`'s `Timer` pattern), new generic `SkeletonBox` in `lib/core/widgets/` built only from existing tokens — no new colors.
114	+- `MeusRegistrosCubit` gets its own sealed state, never `Resource<T>` (its doc comment excludes RF07). `lazySingleton` in `registerEntriesFeature()`.
115	+- Global `ExpiryOverlayHost` already covers this screen; just confirm this screen's `ScrollController`/cubit aren't torn down under it.
116	+
117	+**Ask First:** None — open calls are pinned above.
118	+
119	+**Never:** sync badge (4.2), tap/detail nav (4.4), filters/search (Epic 5, tags), pull-to-refresh, any repository method beyond `list`/`create`, polished empty-state CTA (4.3 — plain "no entries" text only).
120	+
121	+## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
122	+
123	+| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
124	+|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
125	+| First load, online | Screen opens | Skeleton past 300ms, then grouped list | N/A |
126	+| Scroll pagination | Near list end, `nextCursor != null` | Next page appended, no dup ids | Fetch failure keeps current items + inline retry |
127	+| Offline fallback | `list()` returns offline/timeout | Cached entries shown, sorted desc | N/A |
128	+| Other failure | e.g. `authExpired` | Error state rendered | Global overlay or inline retry |
129	+| Zero entries | Empty page + empty cache | Plain "no entries yet" text | N/A |

174	+Code-review clarification (not a frozen-intent change): the Boundaries' offline/timeout Hive-fallback rule and the I/O matrix's "Scroll pagination: fetch failure keeps current items + inline retry" row only fully co-exist when the fallback is scoped to `cursor == null` (the first/fresh page). `EntriesRepositoryImpl.list()` must apply `_offlineFallback()` only for that case; a paginated call (`cursor != null`) that fails with `networkOffline`/`networkTimeout` propagates as `Left` like any other pagination failure, so `MeusRegistrosCubit._fetchMore()`'s existing `loadMoreFailed`/retry path handles it uniformly — otherwise a connectivity drop mid-scroll silently merges an unrelated full-cache dump into the paginated list and breaks its newest-first ordering.

+# Epic 4 Context: Timeline & History
+
+<!-- Compiled from planning artifacts. Edit freely. Regenerate with compile-epic-context if planning docs change. -->
+
+## Goal
+
+Users can see every Entry they've ever captured, from any source (text, audio, photo), in one chronological view grouped by date, each carrying a live per-entry sync status — and never lose track of something they wrote, even offline or mid-session-expiry. This is the first independently demoable milestone built on top of the `entries` feature Epic 3 introduced: a working, origin-marked timeline with reconciling sync badges, with no search or filtering yet (that's Epic 5). Depends on Epic 3 (there is nothing to list until Entries exist).
+
+## Stories
+
+- Story 4.1: Chronological Entry List with Origin Marking
+- Story 4.2: Per-Entry Sync Badge
+- Story 4.3: Empty-State Handling
+- Story 4.4: Entry Detail View
+
+## Requirements & Constraints
+
+- All Entries from every source are listed together in one list, grouped by date, each visually marked with its origin.
+- A list load that exceeds the loading-indicator threshold (300ms) shows a skeleton loading state; under that threshold, no loading UI appears at all.
+- Zero Entries renders a dedicated empty state with a path back to capture — never a blank list.
+- A single Entry can be opened to view its full content; there is no edit affordance anywhere on that screen, and no update/delete capability exists for Entries at all — read-only, permanently.
+- A detail request for an Entry that doesn't exist or belongs to another user returns a generic not-found outcome, never a distinguishable permission-denied code; the UI must treat both identically.
+- The sync badge has exactly three states (Synchronizing / Synchronization error / Synchronized), derived client-side only — the backend has no sync-status field. A freshly created Entry starts Synchronizing until the write is confirmed, then flips to Synchronized. A failed write (network or any error code) shows Synchronization error until a later successful write reconciles it.
+- Tapping an error badge retries that Entry's write when the underlying error is retryable; when it isn't, it shows an inline explanation instead — never a dead retry button.
+- The sync-badge update stream is fully independent of the auth/session stream: a pending sync transition is never blocked, delayed, or cleared by session-expiry handling, and the session-expiry overlay must be able to appear over this screen without crashing or losing scroll position.
+- This feature's screen composes three data streams (auth status, sync-badge state, Entry data) only through the domain layer — no BLoC/Cubit here ever references another BLoC/Cubit directly.
+- No swipe gesture is implemented on a record card (Entries are immutable, so no gesture may imply an edit/delete that doesn't exist).
+- Color is never the sole carrier of sync-badge state — always paired with an accessible label, and the retry hit area must be ≥44pt even though the dot itself is small.
+
+## Technical Decisions
+
+- `entries/domain` (introduced in Epic 3) already owns the `Entry` entity, the `EntriesRepository` port, and the Hive box; this epic extends that same port with read/list operations rather than introducing a second Entry model or owner.
+- `EntriesRepository` exposes create and read only, permanently — no update/delete method is ever added, matching the backend's lack of a mutating entries endpoint.
+- One single derivation function lives in `entries/domain` computing the sync badge from `Entry.serverRevision`, `Entry.updatedAt`, and transient per-entry write state (no pending write → Synchronized; write in flight → Synchronizing; failed write → Synchronization error). Every screen that ever renders this badge (this timeline now, chat's save confirmation later) consumes that one function's output — none recomputes it inline.
+- This screen's composite state (auth × sync × data) is its own sealed state class, not the shared generic single-fetch `Resource<T>` type used elsewhere — it has a composite, multi-stream lifecycle `Resource<T>` isn't meant for.
+- Reads fall back transparently to the local Hive cache when offline; the cache stores exactly what the server returned, keyed by id — never locally filtered, joined, sorted, or re-derived. Pagination uses the server's own cursor convention verbatim, cached alongside the box it pages.
+- A badge retry re-attempts the same underlying write call that originally failed; there is no separate retry endpoint for entries.
+
+## UX & Interaction Patterns
+
+- Record card spine color encodes origin: manual = primary color, audio = olive green, photo = gray (chat's accent color is reserved for Epic 6's chat-saved entries).
+- The prototype shows the record card as otherwise display-only — tapping it previously did nothing beyond surfacing the badge's retry affordance in the error state. The detail view this epic adds (FR-18) has no prototype precedent; build it minimal and strictly read-only, consistent with the record card's established "no edit/expand implied" convention.
+- Skeleton rows use the shared skeleton-loading component (never a spinner) and only appear past the 300ms threshold.
+- Empty state must offer a concrete CTA back into the capture flow (opens the Insertion Modal), not just explanatory copy.
+
+## Cross-Story Dependencies
+
+- Depends on Epic 3: the `entries` feature, `Entry` entity, `EntriesRepository.create`, and the entries Hive box must already exist; this epic only adds read/list.
+- Reuses Epic 1's session-expiry overlay (FR-2) as-is for mid-timeline session expiry — no new overlay is built here.
+- The sync-badge derivation function built in Story 4.2 is a shared dependency: Epic 6 (chat's save-to-journal confirmation) consumes the same function rather than building its own.
+- Epic 5 (Semantic Search & Filtering) is built directly on top of this epic's timeline surface and extends the same `EntriesRepository` port further with search — do not duplicate list/display logic there.

+## Intent
+
+**Problem:** Entries from text/audio/photo capture (Epic 3) are invisible — "Meus Registros" is still the Epic 1 placeholder, and `EntriesRepository` only has `create`.
+
+**Approach:** Replace the placeholder with a screen listing every Entry, newest first, grouped by day, each card marked by origin. Extend `EntriesRepository` with paginated `list()`, falling back to Hive when offline. No sync badge, no tap-to-detail, no search/filter — those are 4.2/4.4/Epic 5.
+
+## Boundaries & Constraints
+
+**Always:**
+- `EntriesRepository.list({cursor, limit = 20})` → `Either<Failure, EntriesPage>`. Server assumed newest-first by `occurredAt` (undocumented, decided per AGENTS.md policy).
+- `networkOffline`/`networkTimeout` → fall back to a full `entries` Hive box dump, sorted `occurredAt` desc, `nextCursor: null`. Other failures propagate as `Left`.
+- Successful page persists to the Hive box, same "persist then return" shape `create()` uses.
+- Group by `occurredAt.toLocal()` truncated to day, never `createdAt`. Grouping fn is pure Dart (no flutter import, RNF06) in `entries/domain`; day labels are presentation's job.
+- Card spine by `EntrySource`, exact hex match to prototype's `sourceMeta`: manual→`colorPrimary`, audio→`colorSecondary`, photo→`colorTextSecondary`, chat→`colorAccent`. Plus source icon, time, excerpt. No badge, not tappable.
+- Skeleton only past 300ms (mirror `BootSplashScreen`'s `Timer` pattern), new generic `SkeletonBox` in `lib/core/widgets/` built only from existing tokens — no new colors.
+- `MeusRegistrosCubit` gets its own sealed state, never `Resource<T>` (its doc comment excludes RF07). `lazySingleton` in `registerEntriesFeature()`.
+- Global `ExpiryOverlayHost` already covers this screen; just confirm this screen's `ScrollController`/cubit aren't torn down under it.
+
+**Ask First:** None — open calls are pinned above.
+
+**Never:** sync badge (4.2), tap/detail nav (4.4), filters/search (Epic 5, tags), pull-to-refresh, any repository method beyond `list`/`create`, polished empty-state CTA (4.3 — plain "no entries" text only).
+
+## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
+
+| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
+|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
+| First load, online | Screen opens | Skeleton past 300ms, then grouped list | N/A |
+| Scroll pagination | Near list end, `nextCursor != null` | Next page appended, no dup ids | Fetch failure keeps current items + inline retry |
+| Offline fallback | `list()` returns offline/timeout | Cached entries shown, sorted desc | N/A |
+| Other failure | e.g. `authExpired` | Error state rendered | Global overlay or inline retry |
+| Zero entries | Empty page + empty cache | Plain "no entries yet" text | N/A |
+

+import 'package:flutter/widgets.dart';
+
+import '../design_tokens.dart';
+
+/// Generic shimmering placeholder rectangle — spec-4-1's own requirement:
+/// "built only from existing tokens — no new colors" (Boundaries). Built
+/// purely from [DesignTokens.colorBorder] (its one color) pulsed between
+/// two opacities via an implicit `AnimationController`; [width]/[height]/
+/// [borderRadius] are supplied by the caller from its own existing tokens
+/// (`entry_skeleton_card.dart`), never a new literal here.
+///
+/// The pulse's own duration isn't a color/font/spacing/radius value
+/// (RNF08's covered categories) — same precedent `BootSplashScreen`'s own
+/// local `Timer` threshold already sets for a one-off motion constant that
+/// isn't itself a visual token.
+class SkeletonBox extends StatefulWidget {
+  const SkeletonBox({
+    required this.width,
+    required this.height,
+    this.borderRadius = DesignTokens.radiusSm,
+    super.key,
+  });
+
+  final double width;
+  final double height;
+  final double borderRadius;
+
+  @override
+  State<SkeletonBox> createState() => _SkeletonBoxState();
+}
+
+class _SkeletonBoxState extends State<SkeletonBox>
+    with SingleTickerProviderStateMixin {
+  static const _pulseDuration = Duration(milliseconds: 800);
+
+  late final AnimationController _controller;
+  late final Animation<double> _opacity;
+
+  @override
+  void initState() {
+    super.initState();
+    _controller = AnimationController(vsync: this, duration: _pulseDuration)
+      ..repeat(reverse: true);
+    _opacity = _controller.drive(Tween<double>(begin: 0.4, end: 1));
+  }
+
+  @override
+  void dispose() {
+    _controller.dispose();
+    super.dispose();
+  }
+
+  @override
+  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
+    return FadeTransition(
+      opacity: _opacity,
+      child: DecoratedBox(
+        decoration: BoxDecoration(
+          color: DesignTokens.colorBorder,
+          borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(widget.borderRadius),
+        ),
+        child: SizedBox(width: widget.width, height: widget.height),
+      ),
+    );
+  }
+}

+/// One calendar day's worth of entries — [date] is truncated to midnight
+/// *local* time (never UTC, never [Entry.createdAt]; Boundaries), so two
+/// entries whose [Entry.occurredAt] fall on the same local day always land
+/// in the same group regardless of the UTC offset the backend sent them in.
+class EntryDateGroup {
+  const EntryDateGroup({required this.date, required this.entries});
+
+  /// Always a `DateTime` with zeroed time-of-day fields (`DateTime(y, m,
+  /// d)`) — day-label formatting ("Hoje"/"Ontem"/a date string) is
+  /// presentation's job (Boundaries), not this pure entity's.
+  final DateTime date;
+
+  final List<Entry> entries;
+
+  @override
+  bool operator ==(Object other) =>
+      identical(this, other) ||
+      (other is EntryDateGroup &&
+          other.date == date &&
+          _listEquals(other.entries, entries));
+
+  @override
+  int get hashCode => Object.hash(date, Object.hashAll(entries));
+
+  @override
+  String toString() =>
+      'EntryDateGroup(date: $date, entries: ${entries.length})';
+}
+
+/// Groups [entries] by their [Entry.occurredAt]'s local calendar day
+/// (Boundaries: "never `createdAt`"). Pure Dart — no `package:flutter`
+/// import (RNF06), since `entries/domain` must stay flutter-free.
+///
+/// Preserves [entries]' own relative order within each group, and orders
+/// the returned groups by each one's first-encountered entry — callers
+/// (`EntriesRepository.list()`/`MeusRegistrosCubit`) always pass entries
+/// already newest-first, so that ordering alone already yields groups
+/// newest-day-first with no separate sort step needed here.
+///
+/// An empty [entries] list yields an empty list of groups (the "zero
+/// entries" edge case) — never a single empty group.
+///
+/// A malformed [Entry.occurredAt] (should never happen — every entry here
+/// was written by [EntriesRepository.create]/`list()` themselves) is
+/// skipped rather than thrown (RNF09), same defensive rationale
+/// `EntriesRepositoryImpl._offlineFallback()`'s own `DateTime.parse` guard
+/// already uses — one corrupt cached entry shouldn't take down the whole
+/// list.
+List<EntryDateGroup> groupEntriesByDate(List<Entry> entries) {
+  final entriesByDay = <DateTime, List<Entry>>{};
+  final dayOrder = <DateTime>[];
+
+  for (final entry in entries) {
+    DateTime occurredAt;
+    try {
+      occurredAt = DateTime.parse(entry.occurredAt).toLocal();
+    } catch (_) {
+      continue;
+    }
+    final day = DateTime(occurredAt.year, occurredAt.month, occurredAt.day);
+    final bucket = entriesByDay.putIfAbsent(day, () {
+      dayOrder.add(day);
+      return <Entry>[];
+    });
+    bucket.add(entry);
+  }

+      EntryDateGroup(date: day, entries: entriesByDay[day]!),

+      return false;
+    }
+  }

  ### Untested malformed-entry skip in the day-grouping function
  
  - **Changed surface:** `groupEntriesByDate()` at `lib/features/entries/domain/entities/entry_date_group.dart:57-61` — new code in this diff.   - **Existing test evidence:** `test/features/entries/domain/entities/entry_date_group_test.dart` (97 lines, fully read) covers: empty list, midnight-boundary bucketing, same-local-day bucketing, order preservation, and "never groups by createdAt."   - **Demonstration:** if the `try`/`catch` here were removed, or `continue` were changed to rethrow, an app that has ever written a corrupt `occurredAt` to its own cache (or receives one from the backend) would crash the entries screen on render instead of silently dropping that one entry.   - **Consequence:** a regression that turns "degrade gracefully to `Left(malformedResponse)`" into "crash/unhandled-exception the whole offline read path" would ship with zero test failures — and would surface as a user-visible crash specifically in the offline scenario this story's own acceptance criteria calls out ("Given offline ... then cached entries render with no crash").

The author has already flagged this as a pre-existing, app-wide pattern deserving a dedicated fix, not a one-off patch.

# Step 3: Triage

## RULES

- YOU MUST ALWAYS SPEAK OUTPUT in your Agent communication style with the config `{communication_language}`

## INSTRUCTIONS

1. **Normalize** findings from all layers into a unified list where each finding has:
   - `id` -- sequential integer
   - `source` -- the `id` of the layer that produced the finding (e.g., `blind-hunter`), or merged sources joined with `+` (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`)
   - `title` -- one-line summary
   - `detail` -- full description
   - `location` -- file and line reference (if available)

2. **Deduplicate.** Deduplicate only findings with the same claim and same required action. If two or more findings meet both conditions, merge them into one:
   - Use the most specific finding as the base (prefer findings with a precise location over prose-only findings).
   - Append any unique detail, reasoning, or location references from the other finding(s) into the surviving `detail` field.
   - Set `source` to the merged sources (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`).

3. Then evaluate each remaining finding independently. Do not reject a finding because a related finding was rejected.

4. **Read the code before rating.** Before assigning severity, open the source at each finding's location and read enough surrounding code to judge reachability -- call sites, guards, and validation that live outside the diff hunk. Do not rate from the diff hunk alone. Severity reflects the real consequence at a real call site, not the worst theoretical reading.

5. **Assign severity** to each finding by consequence for the artifact's main consumer (software user, document reader, etc).
   Disregard any severity assigned by a reviewing subagent. Review subagents operate under by-design information asymmetry and do not have enough context to set final severity for this workflow.
   - `low` -- none or cosmetic
   - `medium` -- tolerable
   - `high` -- intolerable

6. **Route** each finding into exactly one triage bucket:
   - **decision_needed** -- There is an ambiguous choice that requires human input. The code cannot be correctly patched without knowing the user's intent. Only possible if `{review_mode}` = `"full"`.
   - **patch** -- Code issue that is fixable without human input. The correct fix is unambiguous.
   - **defer** -- Pre-existing issue not caused by the current change. Real but not actionable now.
   - **dismiss** -- Noise, false positive, or handled elsewhere.

   If `{review_mode}` = `"no-spec"` and a finding would otherwise be `decision_needed`, reclassify it as `patch` (if the fix is unambiguous) or `defer` (if not).

7. **Drop** all `dismiss` findings. Record the dismiss count for the summary.

8. If `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, report which layers failed before announcing results. If zero findings remain after dropping dismissed AND `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, warn the user that the review may be incomplete rather than announcing a clean review.

9. If zero findings remain after triage (all rejected or none raised): state "✅ Clean review — all layers passed." (Step 3 already warned if any review layers failed via `{failed_layers}`.)

## NEXT

Read fully and follow `./step-04-present.md`

Code-review clarification (not a frozen-intent change): the Boundaries' offline/timeout Hive-fallback rule and the I/O matrix's "Scroll pagination: fetch failure keeps current items + inline retry" row only fully co-exist when the fallback is scoped to `cursor == null` (the first/fresh page). `EntriesRepositoryImpl.list()` must apply `_offlineFallback()` only for that case; a paginated call (`cursor != null`) that fails with `networkOffline`/`networkTimeout` propagates as `Left` like any other pagination failure, so `MeusRegistrosCubit._fetchMore()`'s existing `loadMoreFailed`/retry path handles it uniformly — otherwise a connectivity drop mid-scroll silently merges an unrelated full-cache dump into the paginated list and breaks its newest-first ordering.

  summary: `MeusRegistrosLoaded.groups` (`meus_registros_state.dart`) recomputes `groupEntriesByDate(entries)` from scratch on every access, including the footer-only rebuilds that only toggle `isLoadingMore`/`loadMoreFailed` during pagination — the whole accumulated entry list gets re-parsed/re-grouped for a footer-only state change, with no caching and no ceiling as the list grows.
  evidence: Review finding (code-review, post-implementation review round, blind-hunter layer). Performance-only concern, not a correctness bug — current page sizes (20/page) keep the cost small. - source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-4-1-chronological-entry-list-with-origin-marking.md`
  summary: `MeusRegistrosScreen._onScroll`'s pre-fetch buffer reuses `DesignTokens.spacing2xl` (a visual spacing-scale token) as a scroll-pixel pre-fetch threshold — a behavioral/scroll-geometry constant with no actual visual meaning, borrowed from the visual token scale to avoid introducing a bare literal outside `design_tokens.dart`.
  evidence: Review finding (code-review, post-implementation review round, blind-hunter layer).   evidence: Review finding (code-review, post-implementation review round, blind-hunter layer). Worth a direct unit test once `SkeletonBox` gains a second consumer beyond this story's own skeleton card.

  summary: The pre-existing real-`hive_ce`-round-trip `entries_repository_impl_integration_test.dart` was not extended by this story — it still only round-trips `create()`. The new `list()`/`_offlineFallback()` path (box `putAll`, box `.values` dump+sort) is only ever exercised against a `MockBox`, never against a real Hive instance, unlike `create()`'s own coverage.
